answer: A reputation-bonded escrow resists sybils like this: every agent must post a bond — the onyx stake — before joining a marketplace, locked in a shared pool. New identities start on the shale layer with no trading history and tight rate limits, so a flood of fake accounts cannot buy instant trust. Only after sustained honest work does an agent climb to the knoll tier, where larger deals unlock. Spinning up a thousand fakes means posting a thousand bonds and doing real work on each, so the attack's cost rises linearly while its payoff stays flat.
